nodes.content: Enable speech–gesture reference resolution that distinguishes gesture-dependent meaning from speaker-specific correlations under uncertain cross-modal timing.
requirements: Achieve ≥10 percentage-point accuracy gains over speech-only models on gesture-dependent references from unseen speakers.
Limit accuracy degradation to 5 percentage points under irrelevant-gesture substitutions and ±300-millisecond audiovisual offsets.

nodes.content: Train a speaker-adversarial, relevance-gated grounding model using counterfactual gesture substitutions and latent ±300-ms alignment marginalization.
Does speaker-adversarial training preserve referential gesture cues while relevance gating rejects distractors under ±300-ms alignment uncertainty?
On unseen speakers, adversarial alignment-marginalized gating beats speech-only by ≥10 points; irrelevant gestures or ±300-ms offsets cost ≤5 accuracy points.
Build speaker-disjoint, 30-speaker ReferGesture-1K; compare speech-only, full, adversarial-free, and gate-free models on gesture-dependent, swapped-gesture, and ±300-ms-offset trials.
Train four models on 24 ReferGesture-1K speakers; measure accuracy on six held-out speakers under gesture-dependent, irrelevant-substitution, and ±300-ms-offset conditions.
On held-out ReferGesture-1K speakers, gesture-dependent accuracy was 76% versus speech-only’s 68%; irrelevant substitutions cost 7 points.
Compare full, adversarial-free, and gate-free models on held-out speakers; stratify accuracy losses by gesture substitution and ±300-ms offset.
At ±300-ms offsets, full-model accuracy fell 3 points from 76%; gate-free accuracy fell 9 points.
Which gesture–speech mismatches cause the gate to trust irrelevant gestures, limiting unseen-speaker gains and substitution robustness?
Match n5 substitution failures to n7 offset-stable trials by speaker and utterance; inspect gate weights and semantic mismatch types.
Match n5 substitution errors to n7 offset-stable trials; annotate referent conflicts, pointing similarity, and gate activation.
ReferGesture-1K failure atlas pairing substitution errors with offset-stable trials, including mismatch labels, pointing similarity, gate activations, and predictions.
Train a referent-consistency critic using atlas-labeled mismatch negatives, speaker-balanced contrastive pairs, and temporal jitter augmentation.
Can the critic reject conflicting pointing without suppressing valid cues for unseen speakers under ±300-ms offsets?
On held-out ReferGesture-1K speakers, the critic raises gesture-dependent accuracy to ≥78% and caps substitution and offset losses at 5 points.
Train atlas-negative critic on 24 speakers; test six held-out speakers against 68% speech-only and 76% full-model baselines under substitutions/±300-ms offsets.
On held-out speakers, critic accuracy reached 79% versus speech-only’s 68%; irrelevant substitutions cost 4 points and ±300-ms offsets 3.
Track scene objects and rerank speech candidates using speaker-invariant pointing geometry marginalized over timing; fall back on uncertain intersections.
Stratify failure-atlas substitutions by referent conflict, pointing overlap, and gate activation; compare error rates before and after geometry-based fallback.
Using the ReferGesture-1K failure atlas, stratify conflicting substitutions by pointing overlap and gate activation; compare fallback versus baseline accuracy.
ReferGesture-1K error-strata table comparing geometry-fallback and baseline accuracy by pointing overlap and gate activation on conflicting substitutions.
Audit error-strata table for pointing-overlap errors, then benchmark geometry fallback on six held-out speakers under substitutions and ±300-ms offsets.
On held-out speakers, geometry fallback reached 80% gesture-dependent accuracy versus speech-only’s 68%; substitution and ±300-ms-offset losses were 4 points.
Ablate object tracking and pointing rays; compare referent accuracy and substitution losses on six held-out speakers at ±300-ms offsets.
On occluded-object trials at ±300-ms offsets, substitutions cost geometry fallback 9 points versus 3 without pointing rays.
Can visibility-aware confidence trigger speech fallback on occluded pointing rays without sacrificing gains from clearly visible gestures?
Calibrate visibility confidence; compare fallback versus geometry reranking by accuracy on held-out visible/occluded substitutions and ±300-ms offsets.
Given n20’s gains and n22’s occlusion failures, calibrate visibility-triggered fallback on development speakers; test visible/occluded held-out substitution accuracy.
Visibility-fallback report specifying a calibrated confidence threshold and held-out accuracy by occlusion, gesture substitution, and ±300-ms offset.
Train a counterfactual reference scorer with speaker-timbre randomization, temporal-window pooling, and calibrated speech fallback for low-relevance gestures.
Calibrate counterfactual-scorer fallback using ray-visibility estimates, then compare occluded-substitution robustness and visible-gesture gains at ±300-ms offsets.
Compare p4’s counterfactual scorer against n26’s calibrated visibility fallback on six held-out speakers across visible/occluded substitutions and ±300-ms offsets.
Held-out accuracy reached 81% versus speech-only’s 68%; occluded substitutions cost 3 versus visibility-fallback’s 5 points; ±300-ms offsets cost 3.
Ablate relevance-gated fallback and temporal-window pooling; measure visible and occluded substitution accuracy on unseen speakers at ±300-ms offsets.
On visible overlapping-pointing trials at ±300 ms, substitutions cost the full model 8 accuracy points versus 4 without temporal pooling.
Train speaker-invariant, event-level gesture matching with overlapping-pointing counterfactuals, ±300-ms timing jitter, and ambiguity-triggered speech fallback.
Can event-level matching separate overlapping pointing strokes from irrelevant substitutions while retaining useful gestures across ±300-ms offsets?
Event-level matching cuts overlapping-pointing substitution loss to ≤5 points while sustaining ≥78% accuracy on unseen speakers at ±300-ms offsets.
Train event-level matcher on ReferGesture-1K; compare p4 and speech-only on overlapping-pointing substitutions and ±300-ms offsets across six held-out speakers.
Evaluate event-level matcher on six held-out speakers: record offset accuracy and overlapping-pointing substitution loss versus p4 and speech-only.
On held-out speakers, event matching scored 79% at ±300-ms offsets; overlapping-pointing substitutions cost 4 points versus p4’s 8.
Using n36’s offset-robust matcher, compare clean accuracy and irrelevant-substitution losses against p4 by stroke duration on held-out speakers.
On held-out speakers, event matching reached 82% clean accuracy versus p4’s 81%; short-stroke substitutions cost 4 versus 8 points.
Stress-test event matching on held-out long-stroke and occluded gestures; measure substitution and ±300-ms-offset losses against clean accuracy.
On occluded long-stroke trials, substitutions cost 9 accuracy points and ±300-ms offsets cost 7, exceeding the five-point limit.
Can occlusion- and duration-calibrated fallback protect long-stroke trials without sacrificing event matching’s short-stroke gains?
Calibrate fallback jointly on occlusion and stroke duration; test long-stroke substitution/offset losses and short-stroke clean accuracy on held-out speakers.
Using n38’s short-stroke gains and n40’s occlusion failures, calibrate fallback; retest short-stroke accuracy and long-stroke substitution/offset losses on held-out speakers.
Duration–occlusion calibration report with fallback thresholds and held-out short-stroke accuracy and long-stroke substitution/offset losses.
Freeze n44’s fallback thresholds; validate on a new six-speaker fold, measuring short-stroke accuracy and occluded long-stroke substitution/offset losses.
On the new six-speaker fold, short-stroke accuracy was 83%; occluded long-stroke substitution and ±300-ms-offset losses were 4 points each.
Adopt duration–occlusion-calibrated event matching: n38 showed short-stroke gains, and n46 reduced n40’s long-stroke perturbation losses to four points.
